chapters.name: Overview
chapters.title: ChatGPT — saved page

chapters.name: Page layout
chapters.title: Page layout
chapters.lead: Click a region of the captured interface to inspect its HTML structure. This is a structural diagram, not a screenshot.

sections.title: The two side navigation areas
sections.body: The saved page has an aside containing two separate navigation regions. One has eight buttons; the other has 62 buttons and eleven links.

sections.title: Main page and composer
sections.body: The main region contains a header and a form. The form has three buttons and four file inputs.

sections.title: A dialog exists in this capture
sections.body: One region has dialog semantics and four buttons. The capture cannot establish how it was opened or dismissed.

chapters.unknown: The wireframe shows HTML regions and control counts, not exact pixels, source React components, or actual click behavior.

chapters.name: Libraries
chapters.title: Libraries and frameworks
chapters.lead: Identifiable libraries from the saved JavaScript and CSS. Open a card for evidence and limitations. Package versions are not established.
chapters.unknown: A marker in a saved bundle does not prove a feature ran. Strong, likely and indicator labels describe evidence strength, not installation records.

chapters.name: Chat interactions
chapters.title: How chat interactions could work
chapters.lead: Inspect real source evidence and candidate chat behavior. Conversation selection, message ancestry and response streaming remain unverified until tested.

sections.title: Editable composer and message action controls
sections.body: The saved HTML contains an editable composer within the form and main-region edit and regenerate controls. Their event handlers and effects are still unknown.

sections.title: What is observable
sections.body: The saved HTML has a sidebar, two navigation regions, a composer form and a textbox role. The saved source contains storage and messaging APIs, but no traced action-to-state change.

sections.title: Proposed model
sections.body: Conversation selection and response progress have separate states. Each candidate transition names the event, guards, possible effects and a way to verify the relationship.

sections.title: Branch semantics are unknown
sections.body: The static ZIP cannot establish whether edits or regeneration create nodes, replace nodes or select alternative branches.

sections.title: Source evidence and open tests
sections.body: The saved code has chat-related identity, parent and streaming syntax. The research backlog separates evidence we already have from real interactions that require a new controlled test.

chapters.unknown: All candidate transitions remain unverified. No live chat identity, request payload, endpoint or account data is published.

chapters.name: HTML
chapters.title: HTML and controls
chapters.lead: See what the saved HTML contains: landmarks, links, forms, buttons, scripts and accessible roles.

sections.title: Main structure
sections.body: The document contains a main landmark, two navigation regions within a sidebar, one form and a dialog.

sections.title: Controls
sections.body: The captured page includes 130 buttons, 26 anchor links, four file inputs and one textbox role.

sections.title: Script loading
sections.body: Seventy-two modulepreload entries and eighteen stylesheet links point to captured resources.

chapters.unknown: The snapshot does not enumerate hidden menus or other routes absent from this DOM.

chapters.name: CSS
chapters.title: CSS in the capture
chapters.lead: Review stylesheet links, custom-property groups, responsive queries and motion rules from the saved CSS.

sections.title: Tailwind CSS markers
sections.body: The CSS includes Tailwind custom-property prefixes and utility layer rules. Inspect the Libraries page for the evidence.

sections.title: Token families
sections.body: Custom properties are grouped into color, typography, spacing and other source-level groups.

sections.title: Responsive rules
sections.body: The captured CSS has media and container rules, including reduced-motion conditions. Actual computed styles were not tested.

chapters.unknown: Computed styles, browser support and actual element-level cascade outcomes were not measured.

chapters.name: JavaScript
chapters.title: JavaScript and imports
chapters.lead: Browse the parsed module import graph and find the JavaScript capabilities actually present in the captured files.

sections.title: Framework and library signatures
sections.body: React, React Router, editing and rendering library markers occur in the JavaScript. See the source-based classification.

sections.title: Parsed static imports
sections.body: The module graph contains 236 literal import relationships among anonymous bundle IDs. This does not prove execution order.

sections.title: Browser APIs
sections.body: Event, storage, worker and network callsites occur in the bundles. Their original feature ownership is not fully recoverable.

chapters.unknown: Real dependency ownership and executed call paths require AST-level proof, source maps or runtime instrumentation.

chapters.name: Components
chapters.title: Component clues
chapters.lead: Compare the observed DOM regions with the limits of identifying original React components in minified code.

sections.title: Known DOM structure
sections.body: Sidebar, nested navigation, main header, composer and a dialog are present as HTML regions.

sections.title: UI libraries
sections.body: Radix UI and ProseMirror markers appear in the code. Their exact React component instances were not reconstructed.

chapters.unknown: The precise source component hierarchy and prop interfaces have not been recovered.

chapters.name: Logic
chapters.title: Events and UI logic
chapters.lead: Listener, observer and hook callsites found in JavaScript. Click handlers were not mapped to individual controls.

sections.title: Events are abundant
sections.body: The saved code contains event listener registrations/removals and mutation, resize and intersection observers. Vendor code can account for repeated patterns.

sections.title: From input to effect
sections.body: A plausible path is input → handler → state update → render, but this diagram is explanatory, not a tested trace for any individual button.

sections.title: Media permissions
sections.body: User-media, display-media, peer connection and AudioContext constructors appear in source. Consent, activation and success remain unobserved.

sections.title: Handlers are capabilities, not verified clicks
sections.body: The saved JavaScript contains listener, observer, animation frame and hook callsites, but the archive contains no trace mapping a captured control to an executed callback.

chapters.unknown: No captured live event trace maps a specific DOM control to its owning JavaScript closure.

chapters.name: Flow
chapters.title: Loading and network
chapters.lead: See preload declarations, static imports, fetch/streaming syntax and how much of the runtime sequence remains unknown.

sections.title: Boot declarations lead to candidate modules
sections.body: The HTML references 72 modulepreloads and an external classic script, all matched to captured JavaScript resources. Syntax-tree imports help construct a candidate graph, not a verified execution timeline.

sections.title: Bootstrap
sections.body: The saved HTML carries route-related state, inline initialization scripts, and references to assets. Their presence is certain; chronological runtime execution is not.

sections.title: Presentation
sections.body: CSS layers, custom properties and responsive rules style application regions; JavaScript libraries may update those regions and control transient UI states.

sections.title: Data movement
sections.body: Fetch, streaming reader and WebSocket-related patterns identify network-facing implementation candidates, not observed server conversations.

sections.title: Streaming code shows proximity, not live dataflow
sections.body: Some source function scopes contain both fetch and stream-reader or abort constructs. Without execution, proximity cannot establish a successful request, endpoint contract or server response.

chapters.unknown: No HAR, browser trace, server log or live timing profile was supplied.

chapters.name: State
chapters.title: Client state and storage
chapters.lead: Storage, channels and worker APIs found in the source. The actual stored values and state transitions were not captured.

sections.title: Initial state
sections.body: The HTML includes serialized route/application data. This supports source-level initialization analysis but private values are never published.

sections.title: Persistence layers
sections.body: Local/session storage, IndexedDB and BroadcastChannel APIs occur in captured bundles. Actual stored data, ownership and expiry are unknown.

sections.title: State transitions
sections.body: Worker/message and browser event patterns suggest cross-component or cross-tab coordination, but no transaction history or live graph was captured.

sections.title: Browser storage and cross-tab boundaries
sections.body: Storage method calls, workers, channel constructors and postMessage signatures appear in the saved code; actual persisted keys, values and messages are not available.

chapters.unknown: This archive provides no reliable record of actual storage transactions or state-machine transitions.

chapters.name: Assets

sections.title: Font groups
sections.body: The ZIP includes three interface sans files and 57 math-typesetting font files.

sections.title: Icon sprite
sections.body: Ninety-two SVG use elements reference a saved sprite, using 23 distinct symbols.

chapters.unknown: Original assets are not redistributed; exact on-screen image use was not verified.

chapters.name: Evidence
chapters.title: Findings and limitations
chapters.lead: Read the source-backed findings. Claims about real execution are kept separate from static observations.

sections.title: A stronger source-evidence tier
sections.body: The deeper phase adds a parsed import graph, semantic DOM nesting and resolved sprite references; it preserves prior weaker string-match graphs separately instead of treating them as equivalent.

sections.title: Observed
sections.body: Statements marked observed_static are grounded in captured bytes or derived structural counts. The label does not imply live functionality.

sections.title: Inferred
sections.body: Cross-cutting architectural explanations use conditional language and should identify which links are interpretations rather than direct observations.

sections.title: Still to establish
sections.body: Module ownership, live control behavior, request outcomes and security enforcement require evidence beyond a static ZIP or stronger parsing of the captured code.

chapters.unknown: Reviewed static findings must not be transformed into claims of verified live behavior.

chapters.name: Research queue
chapters.title: Research tasks
chapters.lead: See what was completed and which questions cannot be answered from this ZIP.

sections.title: Source-rich captures launch deeper work
sections.body: Intake now adds a persistent second-phase task graph when a ZIP is sufficiently rich in files, scripts or CSS. Each task has a research contract and dependency list.

sections.title: Review is not automatic
sections.body: Deeper tasks are not closed by source-token counts alone. The first sixteen have specific structured evidence; the remaining investigations stay queued until supported.

sections.title: Story-first output
sections.body: The purpose of the analysis is to explain how a site's systems relate, not merely produce an ever-growing inventory of code tokens.

chapters.unknown: Queue creation is automatic; performing source analysis and reviewing publication remain substantive work.
